claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs, lines 10-31, re-read today: catch (KeyNotFoundException ex) -> LogWarning(ex, "request for a resource that does not exist") + WriteProblemAsync(context, Status404NotFound, "Not found", ex.Message); catch (ArgumentException ex) -> LogWarning(ex, "request rejected as invalid") + Status400BadRequest, "Invalid request", ex.Message; catch (Exception ex) -> LogError(ex, "unhandled exception") + Status500InternalServerError, "Server error", "something went wrong". The lesson's block is character-identical to lines 10-31.

C# language reference: "When an exception occurs, the runtime checks catch clauses in the specified order, from top to bottom. At most, only one `catch` block runs for any thrown exception. ... A catch clause without any specified exception type matches any exception and, if present, must be the last catch clause."

git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Program.cs: "app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>(); app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>(); app.UseCors(); app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization(); app.MapControllers();" — ExceptionHandlingMiddleware is the first UseMiddleware call, hence outer to every app-registered middleware and the endpoint.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live today: curl -sS -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/1 with db stopped returned "HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error" / "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" and body {"title":"Server error","status":500,"detail":"something went wrong"} — no type, no instance, and application/problem+json overwritten by WriteAsJsonAsync exactly as the corrected claim now states.

Half-true. Docs: "the following middleware generates problem details HTTP responses when AddProblemDetails is called ... DeveloperExceptionPageMiddleware: Generates a problem details response in development when the Accept request HTTP header doesn't include text/html." Program.cs calls AddProblemDetails. Executed on an equivalent .NET 10 app (Development, curl Accept: */*): the dev page answered application/problem+json with type/title/status/detail plus "exception":{"details":"<stack trace>"} — the stack trace is there, but inside a parseable Problem Details body.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Without this middleware the app's own fixed Problem Details body is skipped: in Development (what docker-compose.yml sets) the developer exception page answers 500 and, because Program.cs calls AddProblemDetails, writes a problem+json body carrying the exception's type, message and stack trace; in other environments the client gets a bare 500 with no body.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Code at stage-1: the KeyNotFoundException and ArgumentException clauses call logger.LogWarning(ex, ...); only catch (Exception ex) calls logger.LogError(ex, "unhandled exception"). Nothing in ASP.NET Core imposes this mapping — it is three calls this class makes — so "this app's own convention" is exactly right.

Docs: "UseDeveloperExceptionPage is added first when the HostingEnvironment is 'Development'." and "UseRouting is added second, if the user code didn't already call UseRouting and endpoints are configured". Program.cs calls neither, and docker-compose.yml sets ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development" for the api service. Confirmed in execution: the live stack trace of the minimal app ends at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.DeveloperExceptionPageMiddlewareImpl.Invoke(HttpContext context), i.e. outside the app's own middleware.

issues.text: Executed on an equivalent .NET 10 app (CreateBuilder + AddProblemDetails, Development, throwing endpoint, curl Accept: */*): the developer exception page answered "Content-Type: application/problem+json" with title/status/detail plus "exception":{"details":"<stack trace>"}. DonHang's Program.cs calls AddProblemDetails too, so without this middleware the client still gets a parseable body; what the middleware removes is the exception's type, message and stack trace, not parseability. issues.text: Unlisted claim: "printed with a `fail:` prefix" is a behaviour claim about the console formatter's level abbreviation (fail = Error, warn = Warning, info = Information) and appears nowhere in `.meta.json`. It is true for this app — docker logs donhang-api today showed "fail: DonHang.Api.Middleware.ExceptionHandlingMiddleware[0] / unhandled exception" — but it depends on the default (simple) console formatter, which nothing in appsettings.json changes; a JSON console formatter would print no such prefix. Section 7 and quiz q4 both rest on this prefix.
issues.quote: the `LogError` call puts it in the log, printed with a `fail:` prefix
issues.fix: Add a `behavior` claim to `.meta.json`: "The default console formatter prefixes each entry with a four-letter level abbreviation — `fail:` for Error, `warn:` for Warning, `info:` for Information; verified live in `docker logs donhang-api` at stage-1, with no formatter override in appsettings.json."
